_doc: Registry of every `continue-on-error: true` in .github/workflows/. Read by scripts/verify-ci-gates.ts (`npm run audit:ci-gates`), which FAILS on an unregistered occurrence, a registration missing any field, an expired reviewBy, and a registration whose step no longer soft-fails. A soft-failing step is a gate that cannot fail; this file is what stops one from being added silently or from outliving its reason. Key format: '<workflow file>::<step name>' — the step's `name:`, because line numbers move.
_why: The class this exists to prevent, with a real instance: security-scan.yml ran `npm audit --audit-level=high` with continue-on-error for months, and SEC-021's disposition in the security register named that same audit as its mitigating control. The audit reported a HIGH advisory in @fastify/static on every run — an authorization bypass in the module serving the SPA — and nothing failed. A control configured never to fail is not a control, and citing one elsewhere as a mitigation converts a visible finding into an invisible one.
_rules: A step that IS a gate does not belong here. Make it blocking instead — a red weekly cron blocks no development and is the correct signal.
Every entry needs a reviewBy. 'While we establish a baseline' with no date is how a temporary exception becomes permanent.
The list only shrinks. Removing continue-on-error from a step means deleting its row here; the auditor fails on a stale row so an exemption cannot outlive its reason.

_categories.cosmetic: Writes a badge, a summary or an annotation. The failure has no bearing on whether the code is correct, and failing the run would misreport a reporting outage as a code regression.
_categories.tool-quirk: The tool exits non-zero on a legitimate no-op. Downstream steps already gate on the real condition. Must name the exact quirk.
_categories.reporter-not-gate: The same check runs BLOCKING somewhere else; here it only routes the finding to a channel. Must name where the blocking copy runs.
_categories.platform-limit: Blocked by a GitHub plan or repo-visibility limit rather than by the code. Must name the condition that would lift it.

test.yml::Update test badge.reason: schneegans/dynamic-badges-action writes a gist. A gist 404 or a rotated WEAVER_FREE_GIST_TOKEN would fail the whole test job while every test passed.

test.yml::Update backend test badge.reason: As above — badge write, not a check.

test.yml::Update TUI test badge.reason: As above — badge write, not a check.

test.yml::Update total-tests badge.reason: As above — badge write, not a check.

test.yml::Update compliance-auditors bad.reason: As above — badge write, not a check.

dependabot-labeler.yml::Fetch Dependabot.reason: dependabot/fetch-metadata v3.x exits non-zero with 'PR does not contain metadata, nothing to do.' on legitimately-opened Dependabot PRs (re-opened, amended commits, metadata not yet attached). Downstream label steps gate on `package-ecosystem` being present, so a genuine absence correctly labels nothing. Failing here would misreport a no-op as a regression.

codeql-feedback.yml::Run coverage audito.reason: audit:codeql-coverage runs BLOCKING in test:compliance, where an untriaged rule stops the push. This workflow's job is to surface new rules into a tracking issue; a daily red cron is read by nobody, so failing here is the wrong channel for the same finding.

release.yml::Attest build provenance (PW.reason: GitHub attestations require a paid plan or a public repo. Weaver-Dev is private and the org is on the free plan. Attestations do fire on the public Weaver-Free mirror via release-to-free. Lifts when the org moves to Team/Enterprise, or when this workflow runs on the public repo directly.
